# Psalm 102 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A prayer of someone suffering, overwhelmed, pouring out their troubles before the LORD.

**2** LORD, hear my prayer! Let my cry for help reach you!

**3** Don't turn away from me when I'm in trouble! Listen closely — when I call, answer me right away!

**4** My life is disappearing like smoke; my bones burn like hot coals.

**5** My heart has been beaten down and dried up like dead grass — I even forget to eat.

**6** I groan so much that I'm nothing but skin and bones.

**7** I'm like a lonely desert bird, like an owl sitting in the ruins.

**8** I lie awake at night — like a single bird perched alone on a rooftop.

**9** My enemies mock me all day long; those who ridicule me use my name as a curse word.

**10** I eat ashes instead of food and mix my drinks with tears,

**11** because of your fury and anger — you picked me up and threw me aside.

**12** My life is fading like an evening shadow; I'm drying up like grass.

**13** But you, LORD — you sit on your throne forever! Your fame endures through every generation.

**14** You will stand up and show compassion to Zion — because the time has come to be kind to her. The appointed moment is here!

**15** Your servants love even the rubble of Zion; they treasure even her dust.

**16** Then the nations will honor the LORD's name, and every king on earth will respect his glory.

**17** For the LORD will rebuild Zion and appear in his glory.

**18** He will respond to the prayers of the desperate and will not dismiss their pleas.

**19** Write this down for future generations, so that people not yet born can praise the LORD:

**20** He looked down from heaven, from his holy place on high. The LORD gazed down at the earth

**21** to hear the groans of the prisoners and to free those sentenced to death,

**22** so that the LORD's name would be proclaimed in Zion and his praise in Jerusalem,

**23** when nations and kingdoms come together to worship the LORD.

**24** He drained my strength while I was still young; he cut my life short.

**25** I cry out, 'My God, don't take me in the middle of my life! Your years go on through every generation —

**26** long ago you laid the foundation of the earth, and the heavens are the work of your hands.

**27** They will wear out, but you will remain. They will all fall apart like old clothes. You will swap them out like a worn-out coat, and they'll be gone.

**28** But you never change, and your years will never end.'

**29** The children of your servants will live in safety, and their descendants will be established in your presence.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **102:7-8**: The loneliness imagery is devastating: a desert bird, an owl in ruins, a solitary sparrow on a roof. Suffering isolates — and the psalm doesn't pretend otherwise.

- **102:26-28**: This is one of the Bible's most breathtaking contrasts: the entire universe — heavens and earth — will wear out like old clothes. But God? 'You never change.' That's the ultimate security in an impermanent world.

— PNEUMA
